Possible realities / Laboratory 001

What could
reality be?

We experience a world of space, time, things, and causes. But which of those must exist at the beginning?

This is a collection of small experimental worlds. We change their rules, watch what happens, record surprises, and ask what the results do—and do not—tell us. There is no predetermined answer, and no claim that these models reproduce our universe.

Experiment 004 / rule workbench

Can a tiny rule make something complicated?

Imagine a row of lights. Every new row is determined only by the three lights immediately above each position. Choose a rule, predict what will happen, then run it. No physical universe is being simulated.

Cellular pattern output.

Each horizontal row is one step. Light cells are active; dark cells are inactive. The image is a history of a rule, not a picture of physical space.

Choose a rule and run the experiment.

Rules are standard one-dimensional elementary cellular automata. A rule is an eight-case lookup table, not a claim about nature. Each cell updates from itself and its two neighbors; the left and right ends wrap around.

Scientific boundaries

What would count as a discovery?

A repeatable, surprising behavior in a defined model is a real observation about that model. It is not automatically evidence about our universe. We will distinguish established mathematics, results of our experiments, and speculation. A failed prediction, a boring outcome, or a model that breaks is useful information too.

Earlier investigations: Almost the Same (chaos), Only Between (relationships), and Without Coordinates (distance).

Possible Realities / No theory of everything. Just better questions.
